concepts.name: Relational Model and SQL Overview
concepts.description: Introduces the relational model where data is represented as tables (relations) with rows and columns, SQL as a declarative language, and key concepts: primary keys uniquely identify rows, foreign keys represent relationships.

concepts.name: Data Definition Language: CREATE TABLE with Constraints
concepts.description: Demonstrates CREATE TABLE syntax for defining schema, including column data types and integrity constraints such as PRIMARY KEY and NOT NULL.

concepts.name: Basic Querying: Filtering, Projection, and Ordering
concepts.description: Covers fundamental SELECT query clauses: WHERE for row filtering, SELECT list for column projection, and ORDER BY for result sorting.

concepts.name: Integrity Constraints: Primary Key, Foreign Key, Check, and Referential Integrity
concepts.description: Explains constraint types (primary, candidate, unique, foreign key, NOT NULL, CHECK) that prevent invalid database states, with emphasis on referential integrity requiring foreign-key values to match referenced keys.

concepts.name: Join Operations: Inner, Left, and Self Joins
concepts.description: Describes how joins combine rows from multiple tables: INNER JOIN retains only matching rows, LEFT JOIN preserves unmatched left-table rows, and self-joins compare rows within the same table using aliases.

concepts.name: Aggregation and Grouping: Aggregate Functions, GROUP BY, and HAVING
concepts.description: Introduces aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX), GROUP BY for partitioning rows into groups, and HAVING for filtering groups after aggregation, distinguishing it from WHERE which filters input rows.

concepts.name: Subqueries: Scalar, Correlated, EXISTS, and UNION
concepts.description: Covers nesting queries: scalar subqueries returning single values, correlated subqueries referencing outer query rows, EXISTS for existence checks, and UNION for combining compatible result sets.

concepts.name: Normalization: Functional Dependencies and Normal Forms
concepts.description: Explains normalization to reduce redundancy and update anomalies: 1NF requires atomic values, 2NF removes partial dependencies, 3NF addresses transitive dependencies, BCNF requires determinants to be superkeys, using functional dependency notation X → Y.

concepts.name: Transaction Management: ACID Properties, COMMIT, and ROLLBACK
concepts.description: Defines transactions as logical units of work with ACID properties (atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability), and shows COMMIT to make changes durable and ROLLBACK to discard uncommitted changes.

concepts.name: Concurrency Control: Isolation Levels, Locking, and Two-Phase Locking
concepts.description: Describes concurrency anomalies (dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantom reads), isolation levels, and two-phase locking protocol with growing and shrinking phases; includes explicit row locking via FOR UPDATE.

concepts.name: Transaction Savepoints
concepts.description: Illustrates savepoints within a transaction allowing partial rollback to a named point (SAVEPOINT, ROLLBACK TO) without aborting the entire transaction.

concepts.name: Database Savepoints
concepts.description: A savepoint allows partial rollback within a transaction, enabling later work to be undone without discarding earlier operations, providing granular transaction control.

concepts.name: Database Indexes
concepts.description: An index is an auxiliary structure that speeds row location and query reads, but consumes storage and adds maintenance overhead to writes; column order in multi-column indexes is critical, with leading columns being especially important for query optimization, and EXPLAIN can inspect index choices.

concepts.name: Database Views
concepts.description: A view is a named query definition stored in the database, referenced like a relation; it encapsulates filtering logic and provides reusable query abstractions for improved readability and encapsulation of filtering logic.

concepts.name: Common Table Expressions
concepts.description: A CTE names an intermediate result set within a larger query, improving readability and enabling multi-stage query construction; recursive CTEs can express hierarchical traversals where supported.

concepts.name: Database Triggers
concepts.description: A trigger automatically executes configured logic in response to database events such as INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE; it can enforce auditing or business rules using DBMS-specific NEW/OLD row references.

concepts.name: Stored Procedures
concepts.description: A stored procedure is an encapsulated set of SQL statements with parameters, stored at the database level for reuse; it encapsulates reusable database operations and syntax varies across DBMS platforms.

concepts.name: Entity-Relationship Modeling & Cardinality
concepts.description: ER modeling identifies entities, attributes, relationships, and cardinalities before database implementation; cardinality defines the numeric participation of entities in relationships, and many-to-many relationships are resolved using associative tables.

concepts.name: Database Recovery Mechanisms
concepts.description: Recovery mechanisms restore database consistency after failures using write-ahead logging, checkpoints, and backups; write-ahead logging records changes before data pages are written, checkpoints reduce recovery log processing scope, and backups protect against irreversible data loss.
